content: Levoverbenone is classified as an expectorant and is the L-isomer of verbenone. The southern pine beetle (Dendroctonus frontalis), a bark beetle species, poses a significant threat to pine trees in the southeastern United States. The reproductive cycle of this beetle is regulated by varying ratios of specific natural chemicals, including verbenone. During reproduction, these beetles aggregate in large numbers within their host pine trees. At the onset of an attack, chemicals produced by the infested trees and the beetles themselves attract additional beetles of the same species. However, as the infestation progresses, verbenone is produced, which reduces the likelihood of further beetles landing and attacking the tree. Forest managers often attempt to control infestations of the southern pine bark beetle by cutting down and sometimes burning infested trees along with nearby healthy trees. To protect susceptible healthy trees in the vicinity, they apply verbenone formulations to repel and confuse the beetles. Levoverbenone, also known as (-)-verbenone, is also utilized to manage infestations of the mountain pine beetle (Dendroctonus ponderosae). Verbenone serves as the primary anti-aggregation pheromone for the mountain pine beetle, a forest insect known for causing extensive tree mortality in western North America. Despite its use for tree protection, failures in efficacy are relatively common. However, a specific verbenone formulation, SPLAT® Verb, has demonstrated exceptional efficiency in protecting individual lodgepole pines (Pinus contorta) and small stands of these trees from mortality caused by Dendroctonus ponderosae. Applications of SPLAT® Verb resulted in complete protection of individual Pinus contorta trees, while untreated control trees experienced a mortality rate of 3%. Additionally, significantly fewer Pinus contorta trees were killed by Dendroctonus ponderosae in 0.41-hectare circular plots (11-meter radius) surrounding trees treated with SPLAT® Verb compared to untreated control plots.
